questions.q: Track Changes in MS Word is found under which tab?
questions.solution: Track Changes, Comments, Compare, Protect and Word Count are all on the Review tab.
questions.shortcut: Anything about checking/editing text collectively lives in Review.

questions.q: Which port carries digital audio and video signals over a single cable to a monitor or TV?
questions.solution: HDMI transmits uncompressed digital video plus audio in one cable. VGA is analog video-only, PS/2 is for keyboard/mouse, and serial COM ports carry slow bit-serial data.
questions.shortcut: Audio AND video together -> HDMI (or DisplayPort, if listed).

questions.q: The port that transmits data one bit at a time as a single stream, traditionally used for slow data over long distances, is the:
questions.solution: A serial port (COM/RS-232) sends bits sequentially over one channel - slower but reliable over longer cable runs. Parallel ports send a byte across 8 wires simultaneously but only over short distances.
questions.shortcut: 'One bit at a time / single stream' = serial, word for word.

questions.q: Which key combination ends a running slide show?
questions.solution: Esc exits the slideshow back to the editor (Alt+F4 would close PowerPoint itself; F5 starts a show).
questions.shortcut: Presenting runs until Escape - the universal cancel key.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'Someone is auditing our accounts this week.'
options: Our accounts are been audited this week.
Our accounts are auditing this week.
Our accounts were being audited this week.
Our accounts are being audited this week.
questions.solution: Present continuous row with the vague *someone* dropped: **Our accounts are being audited this week.** 'Are been audited' misplaces been; 'are auditing' leaves the sentence active with the accounts doing the auditing; 'were being audited' shifts to the past row.
questions.shortcut: Continuous active → being + V3; drop the vague agent.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The doctor repeats the passage's controlling metaphor: a market **sells** — and this one sells food but really 'sells company'. *Paints*, *measures* and *imports* are grammatical verbs, but each breaks the selling idea the whole passage runs on. Reading the passage first tells you the writer is still inside the market metaphor.
questions.shortcut: Theme check: the sentence plays on 'market → selling'; keep the verb that stays inside the metaphor.
questions.passage: When the textile mill in Erode added a night shift, hundreds of workers finished duty at two in the morning — and found every shop shut. Within months, a small night market appeared near the mill gate: tea stalls, a barber, a pharmacy and carts selling hot (1) ______. Traders say trust is their main (2) ______: goods are left on open shelves, and payments are dropped into a tin, yet nothing is ever missing. A doctor who volunteers at the market's first-aid desk notes that many workers come not to buy but to talk. 'The market sells food, but what it really (3) ______ is company,' he says. The corporation, which once fined the traders for blocking the road, has now built them a covered (4) ______ with lights and a water tap.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The farmer said, "Alas! The locusts have eaten the entire crop."
options: The farmer exclaimed with joy that the locusts had eaten the entire crop.
The farmer exclaimed with sorrow that the locusts had eaten the entire crop.
The farmer exclaimed with sorrow that the locusts have eaten the entire crop.
The farmer exclaimed with sorrow that the locusts ate the entire crop.
questions.solution: Alas is grief: **exclaimed with sorrow that the locusts had eaten the entire crop** — have eaten steps to had eaten. 'With joy' celebrates a disaster; 'have eaten' stays on the direct rung; 'ate' under-shifts the present perfect.
questions.shortcut: Alas → with sorrow; have + V3 → had + V3.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The shop **will open** at nine every morning.
questions.solution: *Every morning* marks a habit → the simple present: the shop **opens** at nine. *Will open* treats a routine as a one-off future decision.

questions.q: **Madhubani** painting, traditionally drawn by women of the Mithila region, belongs to —
questions.solution: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is from **Bihar**, marked by double-line borders and natural colours. It has a GI tag. Odisha's scroll art is Pattachitra.

questions.q: The **Poona Pact (1932)** on the representation of the depressed classes was signed between —
questions.solution: After the **Communal Award** (1932), Gandhi fasted in Yerawada jail. The **Poona Pact** with **B.R. Ambedkar** replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.

questions.q: The first **Jnanpith Award** (1965) went to G. Sankara Kurup, who wrote in —
questions.solution: **G. Sankara Kurup** received the first Jnanpith for his **Malayalam** poetry collection *Odakkuzhal* ('The Bamboo Flute').

questions.q: The method of election of the President of India and the Directive Principles of State Policy have been borrowed from which country?
questions.solution: Both the DPSP and the method of electing the President (indirect election through an electoral college) were taken from the **Constitution of Ireland**. Ireland also gave the provision for nominating 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
questions.shortcut: Ireland = 'President + Principles' — both P-words pair up.

questions.q: The price of an article falls from ₹250 to ₹200. The percentage decrease in price is:
questions.solution:
Decrease $= 50$ on the original ₹250.
$\frac{50}{250} \times 100 = 20\%$.

questions.q: If A : B = 2 : 5 and B : C = 6 : 7, then A : B : C is:
questions.shortcut: 2 : 5 : 7 is the trap from adding ratios instead of bridging.

questions.q: The population of a town is 96,000. It increases by 25% in the first year and decreases by 20% in the second year. The population at the end of the second year is:
questions.solution: $96000 \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{4}{5} = 96{,}000$ — the chips are reciprocals, so the town is back where it started.

questions.q: Which of the following fractions can be written as a terminating decimal?
questions.solution: $80 = 2^4 \times 5$ has only 2s and 5s, so $\frac{7}{80} = 0.0875$ terminates. The others have 7 ($14$), 3 ($45$, $24$) in the denominator.

questions.q:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series.

**a _ b a _ c a _ c _**
questions.solution: Parts grow by one letter: a | ab | abc | abcd. Blanks in order: a, b, b, d → **abbd**.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**29   14   18**

**38   25   20**

**56   13    ?**
questions.solution: Digit sums: 29 → 11, 14 → 5; 11 + 5 = 16 and 18 − 16 = 2. Confirm: 38 → 11, 25 → 7; 11 + 7 + 2 = 20 ✓. Rule: third = digitsum(first) + digitsum(second) + 2. So 11 + 4 + 2 = **17**.
questions.shortcut: Standard rules dead for two seconds → switch to digit sums and find the constant.

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as the numbers of the following sets. (Operations on whole numbers only.) **(2, 4, 8)** and **(3, 9, 27)**
Numbers are written in the six sectors of a circle. Reading opposite sectors as pairs: **14 – 9**, **11 – 12**, **16 – ?**. Find the missing number.
questions.solution: Each opposite pair sums to the same total: 14 + 9 = 23, 11 + 12 = 23. So 16 + ? = 23 → ? = **7**. (9 copies a neighbour; 25 is 16 + 9.)
questions.shortcut: Opposite sectors → constant sum (or product) first.
